issue: Cocktailsås tagged fish/seafood
why: Rose/cocktail sauce is mayo+ketchup+cream; it is served WITH seafood but contains none. False 'contains fisk'. (Egg tag is correct.)

issue: Whole coconut carries tree-nut property
why: Coconut is not among the EU Annex II tree nuts and coconut-allergy is distinct; this yields false 'contains nötter'. Note inconsistency: sibling coconut rows (flesh, milk, oil) have no tree-nut. Annoying, not dangerous.

issue: Swedish name/context 'snäckor' colloquially also means snails/sea snails
why: A recipe saying 'snäckor' in a seafood context (escargots, sea snails = mollusc) could match this gluten pasta with no mollusc property. Low likelihood in Swedish home recipes but worth a disambiguating alias.

issue: Alias 'lingonsaft' is a different product (lingonberry drink)
why: No allergen difference, but the alias maps lingon drinks to cranberry juice — data-quality noise rather than safety risk.

issue: Swedish name 'stensöta' is a different fern (Polypodium); fiddlehead/ormbunksskott is the intended ingredient
why: Naming error, no allergen impact; could mislabel recipes. Alias 'ormbunksknoppar' is the correct concept.

issue: Fiskbuljong grouped under other/beverage instead of a broth/stock or condiment group
why: Allergen props (fish, seafood, animal-product) are correct, so no safety impact, but 'beverage' is clearly the wrong category for a stock/fond.

issue: Pepparkakskrydda tagged contains-gluten; it is a pure spice blend (cinnamon, ginger, cloves, cardamom) with no cereal component
why: False 'contains gluten' verdict on any recipe using gingerbread spice; annoying over-blocking, not a safety risk.

issue: Mixed vegetables grouped as vegetable/leaf
why: Cosmetic; frozen veg mixes are allergen-clean so no safety impact.

issue: Hemp drink tagged animal-product instead of plant-based/vegan-friendly
why: Hampadryck is fully plant-based; animal-product is not allergen-mapped but is clearly wrong and could mislead vegan filtering.

issue: Plain melon carries animal-product alongside plant-based
why: Contradictory props on plain produce; not allergen-mapped but wrong.

issue: Alias 'husmanskost' means traditional home cooking, not hushållsost
why: Any recipe text mentioning 'husmanskost' would falsely match a dairy cheese — false 'contains mjölk', annoying rather than dangerous.

issue: Jellyfish grouped under protein/seafood/shellfish with generic seafood prop but is neither crustacean nor mollusc
why: Cnidarian, not an EU-14 shellfish; if 'seafood' feeds the combined skaldjur verdict this produces a false 'contains skaldjur' (safe direction, but miscategorized).

issue: Sweet chestnut tagged tree-nut, but chestnut is not on the EU Annex II tree-nut list
why: EU tree nuts = almond, hazelnut, walnut, cashew, pecan, brazil, pistachio, macadamia. False 'contains nötter' for chestnut; arguably conservative-safe, so low severity.

issue: Crushed tomatoes grouped as vegetable/onion-family
why: Should be fruit-veg like other tomato rows (58, 138); passerad-tomat (123) has the same mistake. No allergen impact.

issue: Savoy cabbage grouped as vegetable/onion-family
why: Cabbage is a brassica leaf vegetable, not onion-family; no allergen impact.

issue: Edible insects marked with the 'meat' property and no crustacean cross-allergy note
why: EU novel-food labeling requires a crustacean/dust-mite cross-reactivity warning for insects; the schema has no dedicated prop, but a crustacean-allergic user relying on 'fri från kräftdjur' is a residual risk worth noting.

issue: Alias 'leverwurst' names a different product (liver sausage), and 'medisterkorv' is also a distinct sausage
why: Both aliases are pork-based so allergen impact is limited, but leverwurst/medisterkorv frequently contain milk protein, which medvurst's row (no dairy) would then miss when matched via alias.

issue: Plant-based oat cream grouped under protein/dairy
why: Havregrädde is a vegan cream substitute; props are correct (no dairy, contains-gluten present), but protein/dairy group is a miscategorization.

issue: Passata grouped as vegetable/onion-family
why: Same miscategorization as krossad-tomat; no allergen impact.

issue: Generic aliases 'fläsk' and 'fläskkött' mapped to sidfläsk specifically
why: Allergen-safe (still pork/meat) but 'fläskkött' in a recipe usually means any pork cut, not belly — affects matching quality, not safety.

issue: Alias 'risotto' on plain rice — risotto colloquially means the finished dish (parmesan, wine, butter)
why: A recipe line 'risotto' matched to plain rice could mask dairy/sulfites of the actual dish; low because ingredient lines usually mean risotto rice.

issue: Seaweeds (sea-lettuce, nori, wakame) grouped as vegetable/root
why: Algae are not root vegetables; no allergen impact, cosmetic categorization issue (also seaweed-nori, seaweed-wakame).

issue: Soy cream grouped under protein/dairy
why: It is a plant-based dairy substitute; props correctly omit dairy so verdicts are unaffected, but the group is misleading.

issue: Spinach grouped under vegetable/onion-family
why: Should be vegetable/leaf; no allergen impact.

issue: Spettekaka tagged contains-gluten, but it is traditionally made with potato starch (gluten-free)
why: Classic skånsk spettekaka = eggs + sugar + potatismjöl; the gluten tag is a false 'contains'. Some commercial variants add wheat, so keeping it is conservative — low severity, verify recipe basis.

issue: Ättikssprit tagged sulfites
why: Ättikssprit is diluted synthetic acetic acid, not fermented wine vinegar — it does not contain sulfites. Produces a false 'contains sulfiter' (annoying, not dangerous). Same applies to vinegar-essence-24.

issue: Ättikssprit 24% tagged sulfites
why: Same as the 12% row: synthetic acetic acid carries no sulfites; false 'contains' verdict.

issue: Wheat starch grouped under grain/flour/gluten-free while carrying contains-gluten
why: Props are correct (safe default: non-certified vetestärkelse contains gluten), but the gluten-free group is contradictory and could mislead future edits.

issue: Ättika tagged sulfites
why: Ättika/ättikssprit is diluted synthetic acetic acid, not fermented wine vinegar — sulfites unwarranted; false 'contains sulfiter'.

issue: Name 'äggrom' suggests egg but row is fish roe (props fish, alias fiskrom); ambiguous naming could match egg-yolk contexts
why: Props are correct for roe (fish, no egg); flagging only the confusing id/name which could mismatch recipe text like 'äggula'.
